issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s continued possession and payment of rent after a lease expires do not create a tenancy by holding over merely because the landlord accepts the rent when the tenant remains under statutory protection from eviction and mutual intention to create a new tenancy is not proved.
material_facts: The contractual lease expired by efflux of time.
The tenants remained in possession and paid rent after the lease expired, and the landlords accepted the rent.
The tenants’ continued possession was protected by rent-control legislation.

There was no evidence, apart from acceptance of rent, that the landlords intended the tenants to continue in possession under a new tenancy, and the tenants did not establish that they tendered rent with the intention of taking a new lease.
issues.conclusion: There was no tenancy by holding over because the parties’ mutual intention to create a new tenancy was not proved. The claim that a new tenancy required six months’ notice therefore did not arise, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 116 of the Transfer of Property Act requires a bilateral agreement: the tenant’s continued possession after the lease ends must evidence an offer to take a new lease, and the landlord must definitely assent to continued possession, by accepting rent or otherwise. Where rent-control legislation protects the tenant’s possession, payment and acceptance of rent are not, without more, evidence of that agreement. The Court reaffirmed Ganga Dutt Murarka v. Kartik Chandra Das and applied Kai Khushroo Bezonjee Capadia v. Bai Jerbai Hirjibhoy Warden, Morrison v. Jacobs, and Mangilal v. Sugan Chand; it distinguished Manujendra Dutt v. Purendu Prosad Roy Chowdhury.

rule.if: eviction_appeal and lease_expired_by_term and rent_control_protection and tenant_stayed_and_paid and landlord_accepted_rent and no_proof_of_mutual_intent

predicates.eviction_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal in a dispute seeking the tenant’s eviction.
predicates.lease_expired_by_term: The contractual lease ended when its agreed term expired.
predicates.rent_control_protection: The tenant’s continued possession after the lease ended was protected by rent-control legislation.
predicates.tenant_stayed_and_paid: The tenant remained in possession after the lease ended and paid rent.
predicates.landlord_accepted_rent: The landlord accepted rent paid by the tenant after the lease ended.
predicates.no_proof_of_mutual_intent: The tenant did not establish that both sides intended to create a new tenancy, and acceptance of rent was the only evidence relied on for the landlord’s assent.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal concerns a lease that expired by its term, a rent-control-protected tenant who stayed and paid rent, and a landlord who accepted it, no new tenancy by holding over follows if there is no proof of mutual intent.
